one_line_summary: [Zn3(3-atrz)2(4-atrz)2(SO4)2] shows thermal_stability = 595.15 K for target gas

key_insights.title: Mechanism
key_insights.body: electron transfer from framework conduction band to Fe3+ half-filled 3d orbital → selectivity

key_insights.title: Mechanism
key_insights.body: 3-atrz ligand with μ3-κN1,κN2,κN3 coordination and 4-atrz ligand with μ2-κN1,κN2 coordination → stability

key_insights.title: Design Rule
key_insights.body: [positive] rationally design and construct MOFs with intense luminescence → necessary for obtaining crystalline materials for selective and sensitive Fe3+ detection

key_insights.title: Design Rule
key_insights.body: [positive] select an appropriate organic ligand when constructing the MOF → helps construct MOFs with desired structures and properties

key_insights.title: Comparison
key_insights.body: compound 1 vs previously reported compounds: winner=subject_a on novelty_and_combined_Fe3+_sensing_luminescence_performance

key_insights.title: Comparison
key_insights.body: free 3-atrz ligand vs free 4-atrz ligand: winner=tie on emission_maxima_under_340_nm_excitation

key_insights.title: Failure
key_insights.body: [performance_regression] further heating of compound 1 beyond its stable temperature range: the framework of compound 1 collapses

notable_quotes: The framework is only thermally stable up to 322 °C; on further heating it collapses as the organic ligands are released.
Compound 1 shows strong room-temperature luminescence, emitting at 459 nm under 340 nm excitation.
A new Zn(II) MOF, [Zn3(3-atrz)2(4-atrz)2(SO4)2]n, was solvothermally synthesized from ZnSO4·7H2O with two isomorphic aminotriazole ligands.
